Decision_consequence: Garden revenue $99,748.55, recorded costs $52,954.06 and GP $46,794.49 cover January–June 2026. They are historical observations, not a future no-action forecast.

All 45 product names match, and branch/product prices and costs are constant in the file. Names alone do not establish equivalent recipes, portions, quality, service or supplier terms. Verify these before selecting a reference.

Cost closure is hypothetical. Count savings only where procurement, waste or another expense actually falls. A lower allocated charge alone changes reported branch performance, not Stories’ total cash expenses.
For each product, new cost equals Garden cost less α times its gap to the reference. The same α applies across products. If only some products change, aggregate their actual savings and recompute Gₛ.

v scales units sold, not customer or transaction counts. Product mix, discounts and scenario unit margins stay fixed. No elasticity is estimated. Recompute product-level profit if mix, terms, waste or unit costs change.

Price matching changes list prices to the reference and preserves Garden discount rates. Removing discounts restores recorded discount dollars at fixed quantity. Neither customer response nor future promotion effectiveness is observed.

K includes setup, training, testing, switching, delivery, minimum-order effects and six-month recurring expenses beyond scenario costs. Include additional waste or refunds once only; avoid double-counting amounts already in unit costs or net revenue.
v = 85%, 90%, 95%, 100%, 105% and 110%; K = $0, $1,000, $2,500 and $5,000. These are illustrative stress levels, not forecasts, probability bounds or estimated customer responses.

Results are gross-profit changes less additional expenses, not a full forecast of net profit. Existing fixed overhead is unchanged. Ramp-up delays and affected sales coverage must reduce projected benefits. A short trial cannot establish realized six-month benefit.

Repricing adds modeled price changes to recorded revenue, preserving its $0.755 aggregate rounding residual. Full precision is kept until display. Repeated transactions at fixed prices and costs do not identify demand response or the cause of the cost gap.
